subject: Private vs Dedicated: burst/fallback scaling plan for MedCore pilot
body:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.io>, Eleanor Briggs <eleanor@medcore.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private vs Dedicated: burst/fallback scaling plan for MedCore pilot

Hi team — looping everyone in to align on capacity choices for MedCore's compliance-sensitive pilot. Eleanor, thanks again for the conversation last week. The ask from MedCore: support a HIPAA-equivalent workload with predictable latency (95th <= 650ms) and a firm baseline of ~60 steady concurrent sessions with spikes up to ~220 over short windows during batch ingests and shift changes.

High level options we discussed:
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pool): single-tenant hardware in our isolated tenancy with SLA/uptime guarantees and predictable unit economics.
- Private (customer-managed/private deployment): customer owns the infra (VPC or on-prem), Redwood control plane optional; full data isolation but procurement and ops are on MedCore.

Proposal outline (attached: isolation_burst_plan_v1.xlsx):
1) Baseline (production pilot): reserve 6 x H100-80GB equiv (or 8 x A100-80GB equivalent depending on procurement) in a Dedicated pool to meet 60 steady concurrent sessions for the chosen LLM configuration (Llama-3-34B, Q4_K quantized, avg token output 220). This covers steady throughput and keeps latency headroom.
2) Burst strategy: for short spikes to 220 concurrent sessions, we recommend a two-tier bursting plan:
   - Primary burst: maintained in the Dedicated pool as pre-provisioned 'burst slots' (3 additional GPUs kept hot, billed as burst reserve).
   - Secondary fallback: if Dedicated burst capacity is exhausted, route non-critical traffic to a smaller quantized variant (Llama-3-13B Q4_K) on the same Dedicated pool to preserve compliance and keep P95 latency within 900ms. Note: MedCore requires all PHI to remain on isolated infra, so Hosted fallback is not permitted.
3) Private hybrid option: If MedCore prefers Private deployment, recommend sizing for baseline+burst with additional buffer due to higher ops variance: baseline 8 x A100 + 4 x warm standby machines for burst. Private requires MedCore procurement to provision GPU capacity and networking (NAT, Egress rules) and plan for pre-warming KV caches to reduce cold-start penalties (~5-12s per cold replica).

Key tradeoffs to surface:
- Time-to-live/ops: Dedicated gets you fastest time-to-value and we manage autoscaling and kernel tuning. Private gives ultimate data control but adds 4–8 week lead time for procurement and on-prem network validation.
- Cost: Private typically increases unit cost (vendor margins + ops) but reduces long-term per-token charges if MedCore amortizes on-prem hardware. Dedicated has clearer committed-pricing tiers and Redwood absorbs lifecycle upgrades.
- Fallbacks: Hosted fallback is a non-starter for regulated requests. That forces either internal model downgrades (smaller models) or queueing/backpressure policies.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marissa: confirm commercial posture we can offer for a 12‑month committed Dedicated pool vs a Managed Private onboarding fee + 6-month support retainer.
2) Rishi: can you validate the GPU counts above against our perf lab with the customer's typical prompt distribution? Also provide KV cache sizing and expected cold-start times for both mappings.
3) Eleanor: confirm procurement timing and whether MedCore can run a private pilot in their VPC (we'll need VPN + KMS integration).

I've attached a spreadsheet with modeled latency curves, token cost per hour, and a canonical mutual action plan. Also included a draft SLA exception request for the high-burst window (SLA-exception-request.pdf).

Thanks — Mina

Mina Haddad

On Tue, 19 May 2026 at 11:46 AM, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.io> wrote:
> Mina, quick tech notes after running the perf bench against L3-34B Q4_K at seq_len=1024 and avg_out=220 tokens:
>
> - Realistic sustained concurrency: ~10 concurrent streams per H100-80GB when KV cache hit rates are high (>90%). For L3-34B we see ~9–11 depending on request shape.
> - Burst sizing: 60 baseline -> roughly 6 H100 equiv is reasonable. Spikes to 220 need another ~8 H100 equiv if you want zero model downgrade. That is why the mixed approach (6 baseline + 3 hot burst + model-downgrade fallback) meets both economic and compliance constraints.
> - Cache sizing: KV cache requires ~24GB per replica for the prompt windows you described; pre-warming replicas reduces P95 by ~300–600ms versus cold starts.
> - Autoscaling: For Dedicated, we can configure fast-scaling (scale-up in <60s) but scale-down needs hysteresis to avoid churn. For Private, scale-up times depend on customer infra and image pre-pull policies (we've seen 90s–5min variance).
> - GPU type recommendation: prefer H100-80GB for baseline if MedCore wants headroom for future model upgrades (70–120% perf uplift on the same quantized path). A100 is acceptable for a cost-optimized approach.
>
> I updated the spreadsheet with per-minute cost delta for the three scenarios (Dedicated-only, Private-only, Hybrid dedicated baseline + private overflow).
>
> Rishi

> 2) Private onboarding: one-time onboarding + 3-month managed support retainer while MedCore stands up infra. Pricing here includes a monthly platform fee + advisory hours.

Mina/Marissa/Rishi — thank you, this is helpful and clear. MedCore is risk-averse on PHI and our security team prefers Private deployment. That said, procurement will need a clear committed cost model to compare against Managed Dedicated.

Action items from our side:
- I'll share an initial PO draft (attached: MedCore_PO_20260520.pdf).
- Security requests KMS/HSM details and the SLA-exception form; I've returned a filled preliminary compliance matrix (separate upload to your drive).
- Procurement: target to provision the private GPUs in our VPC within 6 weeks; we'll confirm the exact vendor SKU by EOD Monday.

Request from Redwood: please capture a minimal 'warm standby' recipe (how many warm replicas, required pre-pull images, and KV pre-warm steps) that our infra team can slot into their runbook. Also, because we want to limit ops lift during early pilot, describe a managed-retainer option for the first 90 days.
